implementation_selection.status: Confirmed by exact standard0dc0a6b ROMFS module path and ELF symbols
implementation_selection.correction: Earlier net/nat/hw_nat/ra_nat.c references describe alternate legacy implementation, not established WR1200JS active HWNAT. Do not use its dst_port predicates as active-path proof.

active_source_references.finding: Installs mtk_sw_nat_hook_tx, RX hook NULL, registration/unregistration hooks.
Registration excludes wds prefix, adds named extdev and wifi_hook_if with dev_hold; unregister clears hook slot, dev_put and extif_put_dev. No explicit ra2 exclusion here.
Checks IPv6 policy, skb algorithm/magic/hash metadata, output path resolution, LAN/WAN/EXT membership; binding proceeds through fn and skb_to_hnat_info.
IPv4/v6 postrouting hooks use NF_IP_PRI_LAST; bridge hooks also installed. Placement supports tracing but is not end-to-end firewall proof.

references.finding: extif_put_dev NULLs ext_entry->dev and dev_put; no flow/cache operation in helper.
Eligible device triggers SMA_ONLY_FWD_CPU, invalidates every BIND entry, clears HWNAT cache, schedules SMA rebuild at jiffies+3*HZ. Global flow operation, not per-IoT invalidation.
NETDEV_GOING_DOWN invokes extif_put_dev when not wifi-hook registered, then foe_clear_all_bind_entries.
mtk_sw_nat_hook_tx returns for alg/magic/headroom/hash/bound/reason constraints; writes entry dp and BIND. No explicit IoT source/subnet check.
mtk_ppe_dev_unregister_hook clears wifi_hook_if slot, returns netdev refs and calls extif_put_dev; does not itself invoke global bind invalidation.

flow_lifecycle.limits: Source behavior only; final built module and physical forwarding/cache behavior still unverified. No claim that allowed stable policy leaks.

guard_caveat: WR1200JS source board config line953 CONFIG_RA_NAT_NONE=y
wifi_registration_inventory.conclusion: Inventory alone does not prove compiled Wi-Fi offload or an IoT isolation bypass. Require actual command/macro evidence and HNAT external-interface configuration.

verified_target_guard.finding: Archived actual preprocessed macro records define CONFIG_HW_NAT=1 and CONFIG_RA_NAT_NONE=1; CONFIG_RA_HW_NAT_WIFI_NEW_ARCH not defined in inspected records. Direct source registration inventory not active-path proof.

board_external_devices.limit: Embedded final DTB independently decoded for standard0dc0a6b; this is image configuration evidence, not runtime.

references.finding: external_interface uses read-only seq_file fops (no write) and S_IRUGO. No external interface add through this file.

hnat_set_iif classifies known LAN/PPD/EXT/WAN/ndo_hnat_check; unknown nonbridge input sets INVALID and clears metadata when magic/headroom valid. Bridge input is deliberately preserved, requiring bridge traversal proof.
IPv4 prerouting classifies input before external fastpath, which may consume packet before normal forwarding. Thus pre-routing admission is part of isolation proof.

dynamic_admission.conclusion: Static DTB absence and current macro guards narrow admission; complete br-iot traversal and future mode/driver changes still require gate/runtime evidence.

references.finding: Bridge PRE_ROUTING callback calls hnat_set_head_frags(...hnat_set_iif) on head and frag_list, before its external fastpath branch.
External fastpath requires iface FOE_MAGIC_EXT, not already from extge, unicast destination; may return NF_STOLEN.
Unregistered nonbridge ra2 without ndo_hnat_check becomes FOE_INVALID and metadata cleared if valid/headroom; later br-iot preserves resulting metadata rather than automatically registering it.
Bridge postrouting uses shared postrouting admission with fn NULL, so ingress and destination registration remain material.

bridge_ingress.conclusion: Normal unregistered-ra2 ingress source path is classified before external fast forwarding. Requires verification of actual netdev ops, bridge callback traversal, headroom/metadata initialization and absence of dynamic registration; not universal packet proof.
